text.p: Swedish price label company Pricer has received more fixed contracts for its new system than expected, the company's chief executive officer Erik Danielsson said on Monday.
He said this had increased the chance of the company's breaking even in 1998 as previously forecast.
"We have fixed orders for 250 million crowns for the new system and that is more than we expected," Danielsson told Reuters.
"We have said that we will reach break-even sometime in 1998 and the chances of this have increased."
On Friday, Pricer announced that it received an order from German retailer Edeka for installing a total of 26,000 price tags and 700 signs for fruits and vegetables in two stores.
After deliveries and approval, Edeka intends to order material for another ten stores, the company said.
For the 12 stores, the order will be valued at around 10-20 million crowns, the company said.
Danielsson said the most interesting possibility for Pricer was to supply all Edeka's stores which number around 12,000. He saw this as a strong possibility.
"It is pretty pointless to just have a few stores (with such installations)," he said. "The point is to sit centrally and change prices in all stores."
Danielsson estimated the order value per store at 1-1.5 million crowns.
Another 35-40 stores have bought pilot installations from Pricer.

"They (the stores) have not changed their minds, but are waiting for the new system that will be launched at the beginning of 1997," he said. "The new system means that quite a few things will happen in the near future."
